checks: For p∈A and 0≤t<1, convexity gives A_t⊆A. The shell has volume |A|[1−(1−t)^d], and the fixed cap loss is exactly its intersection with that shell. An almost-everywhere lower bound on A therefore suffices on each shell.

The inverse homothety changes the threshold to (b_i−t v_i·p)/(1−t) and its derivative at zero is b_i−v_i·p. Fubini along v_i/||v_i|| makes the cap threshold derivative −σ_i. At a proper cut the section-volume root is concave by Brunn–Minkowski and continuous in d≥2; in d=1 the interior section has counting measure one. Differentiating the product yields minus the displayed loss and the factor d on the right. The center may be on the boundary; no differentiation in p is required.

Away from the union of forbidden null singleton regions, coverage gives an allowed singleton or a capture set containing a pair. Positive weights make the combined-list minimum valid, including when every singleton is excluded.
In the d=1 check A=[0,1] with the two opposite unit-normal cuts at 1/2 and weights one, the two calculated losses are p and 1−p. They sum to 1=d|A|τ for every center, including both endpoints.

overlap.comparison: It uses subadditivity and coverage for a static three-planar-fiber depth bound, but neither treats weighted loads over a removed shell nor differentiates arbitrary ordinary cap volumes. No accepted equivalent was found.

readability: No ambiguous step. Proper cuts keep v_i nonzero and all section evaluations away from projection endpoints.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The pointwise weighted capture bound integrates over every nested homothetic shell and yields the stated derivative inequality, with any center in A and any proper-cut finite cover.
